# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section A lines 1–25 | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**1:1** [...On the si]xteenth of-it: a sabbath. On the seventeenth [...] On the eighteenth [...]

**1:2** [...] On the twen[tieth of-it ...] On the twenty-first of-it [...]

**1:3** [...] On the twenty-third of-it: a sabbath. On the twenty-fourth of-it [...]

**1:4** [...] On the twenty-fifth of-it [...]

**1:5** On the twenty-fifth of-it: a sabbath. On the twenty-sixth of-it [...]

**1:6** [...] On the twenty-eighth of-it [...] On the twenty-ninth of-it [...]

**1:7** On the thirtieth of-it: a sabbath. On the thirty-first of-it [...]

**1:8** On the first of-the-second-month after the sabbath: the first day. On the second of-it [...]

**1:9** [...] On the fourth of-it [...] On the fifth of-it [...]

**1:10** On the seventh of-it: a sabbath. On the eighth of-it [...]

**1:11** [...] On the ninth of-it [...] On the tenth [...]

**1:12** On the fourteenth of-it: a sabbath. On the fifteenth of-it [...]

**1:13** [...] On the sixteenth of-it: a sabbath. On the seventeenth [...]

**1:14** [...] On the twenty-first of-it: a sabbath. On the twenty-second of-it [...]

**1:15** On the twenty-third of-it: a sabbath. On the twenty-fourth of-it [...] On the twenty-fifth [...]

**1:16** [...] On the twenty-eighth of-it: a sabbath. On the twenty-ninth [...]

**1:17** On the thirtieth of-it: a sabbath. And after it, the first of-the-third-month [...]

**1:18** [...] the days of-the-first-month are thirty days, and the second month thirty days [...]

**1:19** [...] and on the fourteenth of-the-[first]-month between-the-two-evenings is the Passover of-the-LORD.

**1:20** On the fourteenth of-the-[first]-month at-twilight is the Passover of-the-LORD.

**1:21** On the fifteenth of-it is the Festival of-Unleavened-Bread. Seven days shall-you-eat unleavened-bread.

**1:22** On the first day: a holy convocation. You-shall-not do any work of-labor.

**1:23** [...] On the twenty-first of-it: a holy convocation [...] On the twenty-second [...]

**1:24** On the twenty-sixth of-it [...] after the sabbath [...]

**1:25** [...] the days [...] the sabbaths of-the-months [...] the appointed-times [...]

---

*EMET notes: Section A preserves a 364-day solar calendar, diverging from the 354-day lunar calendar of the Jerusalem temple. The term "sabbath" (shabbat) marks weekly rest days in a fixed solar cycle. "Between-the-two-evenings" (bein ha-'arbayim) is the technical halakhic term for twilight, the prescribed time for the Passover sacrifice. The calendar follows a pattern of 30+30+31 days per quarter. Hyphenated forms preserve Hebrew construct chains. Lacunae are extensive in the opening lines; reconstruction relies on parallels across 4Q394–399.*
